# 1 Enoch Chapter 46 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

This log records all verses in 1 Enoch Chapter 46 where the three translators (EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA) significantly diverged in their renderings, along with SOPHIA's resolution and reasoning.

---

## 46:1 — 'Head of Days' — divine epithet from Daniel 7:9 (Ge'ez re'sa mawa'el)

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "One who-had a-Head of-Days" | Literal Ge'ez rendering; preserves the Danielic allusion |
| LOGOS | "One who had a Head of Days" | Same; standard scholarly rendering preserving Dan 7:9 parallel |
| PNEUMA | "someone with a Head of Days" | Lowercase 'someone' to contrast with the exalted title |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** All three preserve 'Head of Days' (= Daniel's 'Ancient of Days'). Adopted LOGOS phrasing. The Ge'ez re'sa mawa'el is the direct equivalent of Aramaic 'attiq yomin. This parallel to Daniel 7 is one of the most important intertextual links in 1 Enoch.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS. Key Danielic parallel — unanimously preserved.

---

## 46:3 — 'Lord of Spirits' — core Enochic divine title (Ge'ez 'egzi'a manafest)

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "Lord of-Spirits" | Literal rendering of the Ge'ez title |
| LOGOS | "Lord of Spirits" | Standard scholarly rendering; possibly = YHWH Sabaoth |
| PNEUMA | "Lord of Spirits" | Same — too distinctive and important to paraphrase |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Unanimous: 'Lord of Spirits' preserved throughout the Book of Parables. This title appears exclusively in 1 Enoch 37-71 and may be the Enochic equivalent of YHWH Sabaoth ('Lord of Hosts'). It must be preserved consistently as a proper divine epithet.

**Status:** Unanimous. Foundational Enochic title — no variation permitted.

---

## 46:4 — 'put down / unseat / topple' — the deposition of kings

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "raise-up the-kings and-the-mighty from-their-seats" | Literal: Ge'ez uses 'raise up' (i.e., lift off) their seats — an ironic reversal verb |
| LOGOS | "unseat the kings and the mighty from their thrones" | 'Unseat' captures the removal with English idiom; 'thrones' for dignity |
| PNEUMA | "topple kings and strip the powerful from their thrones" | Violent, decisive verbs matching the eschatological context |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted 'unseat' (LOGOS). The Ge'ez verb is literally 'raise from' — an ironic lifting off rather than a violent overthrow. EMET's 'raise up from seats' is too literal and sounds like elevation rather than deposition. PNEUMA's 'topple' imports violence beyond the verb. 'Unseat' captures the removal cleanly.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS. Verb semantics — the ironic lifting-off.

---
